cadence: Figures come from authoritative periodic reports — Open Doors World Watch List (annual), Pew Research (periodic), USCIRF (annual), UN bodies, MSF, ACLED and genocide scholarship — plus a verified incident log. There is no real-time global count of people killed for their faith, so this record is refreshed as new reports are published and incidents verified. The page loads this file at runtime, so the record can be updated without rebuilding the site.

debate.topic: Is Nigeria's violence 'religious persecution' — or something more complex?
debate.body: Open Doors and USCIRF frame Nigeria as the epicentre of anti-Christian killing (~3,490 Christians in the year to Sep 2025; ~72% of the global faith-based total). But ACLED, Human Rights Watch and many scholars caution that most of the bloodshed stems from farmer-herder conflict, banditry, kidnapping and land/climate pressure — and kills Muslims as well as Christians. ACLED notes the ~52,900 civilians killed in political violence since 2009 are 'people of all faiths', with Christians bearing a disproportionate share mainly in the Middle Belt. New Internationalist (2026): 'Nigeria's deadly violence is complex, but it's not a Christian genocide.' Both can be partly true — so the record flags Nigeria as CONTESTED rather than picking a side.
debate.src: ACLED · HRW World Report 2025/26 · New Internationalist · Open Doors · USCIRF

debate.topic: How reliable are Open Doors' death counts?
debate.body: Open Doors' method is externally audited each year by the International Institute for Religious Freedom (IIRF), and it says it undercounts because it only uses deaths it can verify. But critics note the criteria are 'home-made' and vulnerable, that attributing any single death to faith (versus general conflict) is inherently hard, and that the IIRF auditor has past ties to Open Doors' own research arm. Treat the figures as a serious, transparent, but advocacy-linked estimate — not a neutral census.
debate.src: Dutch press investigation · IIRF audits · CNE.news

debate.body: No faith is only a victim or only a perpetrator. These records include Orthodox Christian forces killing Muslims (Srebrenica), Hindu mobs killing Sikhs (1984), a Buddhist-majority military killing Muslims (Rohingya), Islamist groups killing Yazidis, Christians and Sufis, a Muslim-ruled state killing Christians (Ottoman genocides), Sunni extremists killing Shia and Ahmadis, and secular/racial ideologies killing Jews, Muslims and Buddhist monks (Nazism, white-supremacism, the Khmer Rouge). The 'by' line on each event names the perpetrator, and flags whether it was another religion, an intra-faith sect, or a secular ideology.

debate.topic: Genocide tolls carry very wide ranges
debate.body: Rohingya: 6,700 (MSF, most conservative) to 25,000+ (HRW / Rohingya groups). Yazidi: 2,100–4,400 (95% CI). 1971 Bangladesh: 200,000–3,000,000, with the Hindu share disputed. Tibet under Chinese rule is claimed in the hundreds of thousands by Tibetan sources and disputed by China. Representative figures shown here are deliberately conservative; the ranges are real and matter.

events.event: Transatlantic slave trade — Middle Passage deaths
events.note: At least ~2 million enslaved Africans died during the Middle Passage; ~12.5 million were trafficked into enslavement, and millions more died within that system.

events.event: Deaths in capture, forced march & enslavement
events.note: Beyond ~1.8–2M Middle-Passage deaths, millions more enslaved Africans died during capture, forced marches to the coast, and within enslavement itself. Scholarly total-loss estimates start around 20 million; a contested minority cites 50–60 million. A deliberately conservative figure is shown; the range is real.

events.event: Racially-motivated mass shootings of Black Americans
events.note: White-supremacist attacks targeting Black Americans: Charleston church (9, 2015), Buffalo supermarket (10, 2022), Jacksonville Dollar General (3, 2023). Counts documented racially-motivated mass killings; the wider debate over policing and everyday racist violence is not quantified here.

The white-minority apartheid regime killed Black South Africans — Sharpeville (69, 1960), the Soweto uprising (~176–700, 1976) and many more. ~21,000 died in political violence overall, though much of the 1990–94 toll was inter-factional; a conservative state-killings figure is shown.

Tens of millions of Indigenous people died after 1492. The largest cause was epidemic disease, but massacres, enslavement, starvation and forced removal were major direct causes. A precise 'killed' figure is not possible — shown for context, excluded from totals.

debate.topic: 'White genocide' is a debunked conspiracy theory
debate.body: Real, documented anti-white racial killings exist in history (British camps for Boer civilians; the 1804 Haitian massacre). But the modern 'white genocide' / 'great replacement' narrative — including claims of a genocide of white South African farmers — is a white-nationalist conspiracy theory with no factual basis, per the SPLC, scholars and multiple governments. White populations are not being exterminated. This record includes documented events, not the myth.

debate.topic: The colonial catastrophe in the Americas was mostly disease
debate.body: The Indigenous population of the Americas collapsed by tens of millions after 1492. The largest single cause was introduced epidemic disease; massacres, enslavement, starvation and forced removal were major direct causes but cannot be given a precise 'killed' figure. It is shown for context and kept out of the totals.

debate.topic: Slavery's death toll spans centuries, not just the Middle Passage
debate.body: Beyond ~2 million Middle-Passage deaths, millions more Africans died in the wider system of capture, enslavement and its aftermath. Any single number understates the toll.

debate.topic: No ethnic group is only a victim
debate.body: The Tutsi were the overwhelming victims of Rwanda's 1994 genocide — but Hutu were massacred in Burundi in 1972 and in Congo in 1996–97. Ethnic mass-killing runs in more than one direction, and this record shows both.

debate.topic: 'Genocide' is legally and academically contested for several cases
debate.body: Whether the Holodomor, the Anfal campaign, or the final Sri Lankan offensive meet the legal definition of genocide is debated by courts and scholars, even where the mass killing itself is not in doubt. Labels here follow the weight of recognition, with the dispute noted.

Bengali 1971 (300,000–3,000,000), Circassian (600,000–1.5M) and Cham (100,000–500,000) tolls vary by an order of magnitude. Conservative representative figures are used, and the widest cases are kept out of the totals.

debate.topic: Abortion — the figures you asked for, and why they are shown separately
debate.body: Worldwide, the WHO estimates ~73 million induced abortions each year (~200,000 a day). In the US, ~630,000–930,000 a year (CDC / Guttmacher); by reported race in 2021 (CDC): non-Hispanic Black 41.5%, white 30.2%, Hispanic 21.8%, other 6.5% — the Black rate several times the white rate. BUT whether abortion is 'the killing of a child or person' is one of the most contested moral, religious and legal questions; there is no consensus, abortion is legal in most countries, and medicine and law generally do not classify it as homicide. These figures are shown as requested DATA, not as a claim that abortion is killing, and are kept OUT of the documented-killings totals above.

Sex-selective abortion and female infanticide have produced an estimated 100+ million 'missing' women and girls, overwhelmingly in parts of South and East Asia. Female infanticide (killing born girls) is documented killing; sex-selective abortion falls under the contested category above. The scale is vast but hard to itemise precisely.

debate.topic: These children overlap the other lenses
debate.body: Most children counted here were also victims in the Faith, Race or Ethnicity records (e.g. the 1.5M children in the Holocaust). This lens re-cuts the same tragedies by age and does not add to the other totals.

abortion.disclaimer: You asked for abortion (the 'unborn child') as a category, so it's here — but strictly as statistics, NOT as a settled claim that abortion is the killing of a child. Whether an abortion ends the life of a child or person is one of the most contested moral, religious and legal questions; there is no consensus, abortion is legal in most countries, and law and medicine generally do not treat it as homicide. These figures are kept entirely separate from every killing recorded elsewhere and are added to no total. This site takes no side.
abortion.usLatestNote: ≈1.13M in 2025 (#WeCount) · ≈1.04M in 2024 (Guttmacher, formal care) — the highest US level in over a decade, risen since the 2022 Dobbs ruling via medication abortion and travel

counter.topic: 'It is / isn't killing' — there is no consensus
counter.body: Most legal systems and roughly half the world do not classify abortion as homicide; many religious and philosophical traditions do regard it as the taking of a life. This site takes no side and does not count it among the killings.

counter.topic: Higher rates among Black women reflect access, not targeting
counter.body: US CDC data show a higher abortion rate among Black women — a statistic sometimes weaponised as 'Black genocide'. Public-health researchers and reproductive-rights organisations attribute the gap to disparities in contraception access, healthcare and income, and reject the 'genocide' framing. It is contested and shown here only with that caveat.

WHO estimates ~73M induced abortions a year worldwide (~200,000 a day). US figures differ: Guttmacher counts ~930,000 (2020); the CDC counts ~626,000 (2021) but excludes several states including California. By-country counts are led by India and China because of population size, not rate.

miscarriage.note: Miscarriage and stillbirth are NATURAL pregnancy loss — not a killing by anyone's definition. Shown for completeness at your request. ~23 million miscarriages a year (~44 a minute; ~15% of recognised pregnancies) and ~1.9 million stillbirths a year (~1 every 17 seconds).

enslavedChildren.note: Enslavement is a grave harm but not a death — shown separately, not as a killing. On any given day today ~12.3 million children are in modern slavery (of 49.6M people total, ILO/Walk Free 2021), including ~3.3 million in forced labour; ~160 million children are in child labour. Historically, roughly a quarter of the ~12.5 million people trafficked in the transatlantic trade were children.
